senses: Synonym of dichromate.
The traditional Korean dress, often characterized by vibrant colours and simple lines without pockets.
ety: Borrowed from Korean 한복(韓服) (hanbok, literally “Korean clothing”).
examples: The Chinese embassy in Seoul defended the decision to include a participant wearing hanbok, describing her as a representative of the country’s dozens of ethnic groups.

senses: Having very little activity; dead.
Genuine; real. Used as a negative intensifier.
Dead serious.
ety: From dead + -ass (“used to intensify an adjective”). Some senses from an ellipsis of dead-ass serious, from dead serious + -ass. Originated in New York City, and popularized around the late 1990s–2000s.
examples: On my way back to town I get to thinking about what Sandee said about Kirby: 'Fix the bastard'. Hmm...maybe we should. After all, what else is there to do on a Friday night in our deadass town?
Yeah, beats this deadass place anyway. I'll go.
Anybody'd come along an' spied you deadass drunk on the plain woulda took yer hair, yer ponies, an' yer stash.

senses: The ovipositor of a female hymenopteran, that pierces.
An Ancient Roman engine for making a breach in a wall.
A member of a church separated from the Church of England; a Protestant dissenter.
Loosely, a Christian who does not conform to the doctrines of an established church.
Someone who does not conform to accepted beliefs, customs or practices.
A noctuid moth (Lithophane lamda).
The state or condition of being unemployable.
Able to be deported.
examples: His criminal convictions — for an attempted robbery in 2003, and for breaking into two parked cars to steal stereos in 2005 — were more than enough to make him deportable.
They repeatedly passed up the invitation to check a list of 96 deportable gang associates active in Nassau County against a local police database that is updated daily, he said.

senses: One who, or that which, prices.
One who engages in the business of laundering.
Wearing or carrying a dagger.
examples: It is true we wear a “dagger,” but we deny ever having been in our life an aggressor upon any man; so that if we be a “daggered assassin,” we ask the Governor to produce the proofs!
Yet in the plenitude of its philanthropy it allows the worse than daggered assassin to enter the home of our adopted citizens, and administer that bane which deprives them of health and life.
Then the dream returned to her, like some daggered thief.

senses: A light cape or short cloak made of silk or lace, formerly worn by women in summer.
ety: Borrowed from French visite. See visit.

senses: A man who crafts santos (religious statues).
An obsolete Scots unit equal to 4 ploughgates, notionally comprising 400 Scottish acres.
ety: Scottish Gaelic dabhach (“vat, large unit of land”); the "land unit" sense may reflect substrate influence on Gaelic from Pictish.

senses: A set of data collected from a single source.
The Monterey cypress, Cupressus macrocarpa.
Not able to be reviewed, or not subject to review
examples: As we emerge from eight years of extravagant executive claims of unreviewable authority, Congress should be especially scrupulous about having a solid legal basis for controversial actions.

senses: Feminist spelling of women.
ety: Eye dialect, also used as a feminist spelling of the word women in order to deliberately exclude the word men.
examples: This is about wimmin sticking together (bois too), and fighting for equal rights and opportunities for everyone, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or sexual orientation.

So eager was I to meet new wimmin-lovin' wimmin—or even just some womyn-lovin' womyn—one didn't need a Ouija board to figure out that I would fling myself forthwith into the world of regional Amazonia.

senses: A small carved or molded figure; a statuette.
ety: Borrowed from French figurine, equivalent to figure + -ine.

senses: Characterized by aberration.
the process of being vascularized.
An office formerly held by Danish and Swedish officials, best translated as governor-general.
ety: Partial calque of Dutch stadthouder (superseded), stadhouder (literally “placeholder”), from Middle Dutch stathouder, itself a calque of Medieval Latin locum tenēns. Doublet of locum tenens and lieutenant.

senses: Furnished with tusks; having tusks.
ety: From Middle English tuskyd; equivalent to tusk + -ed.

senses: Synonym of mathsy (“of or relating to mathematics”).
examples: I showed a draft of this book to one of my nieces and she declared it “too mathy.”

senses: Bringing into subjection or subjugation, and implies the subjugation or pacification of a people, and taking of a pre-populated land.
a spectacular lyric dance drama of southern India performed with acrobatic energy and highly stylized pantomime.
Represented by pictures.
Any large bipedal carnivorous dinosaur, of the family Tyrannosauridae, that lived in North America during the Cretaceous period.
ety: Borrowed from translingual Tyrannosaurus. Doublet of tyrannosaurus
examples: Instead it belongs to a new species of tyrannosaur, which the researchers have dubbed Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis in a paper published on January 11 in Scientific Reports.

senses: To inure; to make accustomed or desensitized to something unpleasant due to constant exposure.
ety: From en- + ure. Variant form of inure.

senses: A token; a symbol; a pledge.
An acknowledgment of a person or thing; an avowal; a profession; a recognition.
ety: From Middle English reconisaunce, from Old French reconissance. Doublet of reconnaissance.
examples: That recognizance and pledge of love / Which I first gave her.
Hobhouse's insolence to Mr. Hunt is not seen in its true light, unless we remember, that the latter is held under heavy recognizances to keep the peace!

senses: Fraud or forgery, or an individual instance of this.
A graduated microscope slide or similar small vessel used for counting or measuring cells
An automated device used for the same purpose
A false albacore.
examples: A pelagic fish, albies have streamlined bodies, and are built to attack prey in short bursts of speed.

senses: Melancholic, dejected.
One who brawls, engages in noisy, unseemly fights.
A beat 'em up game.
ety: From Middle English brawler, brawlere, equivalent to brawl + -er.

senses: A backed, hilted broadsword of the 17th century.
ety: From Italian schiavone, referring to the Slavs of the Doge's bodyguard.

senses: A member of an organized criminal gang in Indonesia.
ety: From Indonesian preman, from Dutch vrijman (“freeman”). Doublet of freeman.

senses: A conical loaf of sugar.
A gratuity given by tradesmen to customers settling their accounts.
A heap of tobacco arranged for fermentation.
Joined by a network, or to form a network.
Large in body; fat; overweight.
ety: From Middle English corpulent, from Old French corpulent, from Latin corpulentus.

senses: Able to be survived.
examples: The conditions they are living in are harsh but survivable.
